description: Implement Profile 5 (Item Control), Profile 6 (MOS Redirection / Story Send), and Profile 7 (MOS-initiated RO Modification). Profile 5: roCtrl (roID, storyID, itemID, command with READY/EXECUTE/PAUSE/STOP/SIGNAL, mosExternalMetadata[]) and roItemCue (mosID, roID, storyID, itemID, roEventType, roEventTime, mosExternalMetadata[]). Profile 6: roStorySend (MOS sends story body to NCS) and roReqStoryAction (MOS requests story action from NCS, per XSD: operation attr, leaseLock attr, username attr, roStorySend child). Profile 7: MOS-initiated roElementAction sent FROM MOS TO NCS - same structure as Profile 4 but direction is reversed. Add unit tests for XML parsing of all profiles.
steps: 1. Create src/internal/xml/control_messages.go with XML structs: ROCtrl (roID, storyID, itemID, command string, mosExternalMetadata[]), ROItemCue (mosID, roID, storyID, itemID, roEventType, roEventTime, mosExternalMetadata[]).

2. Add XML struct for Profile 6: ROStorySendMessage (standalone roStorySend as a top-level message - reuse existing ROStorySend struct but ensure it implements MOSMessage), ROReqStoryAction (operation attr, leaseLock attr, username attr, roStorySend child) - note this is similar to ncsReqStoryAction but travels MOS->NCS direction.
3. Update parser to recognize roCtrl, roItemCue, roStorySend (as standalone message), roReqStoryAction (distinct from ncsReqStoryAction).

4. Create src/internal/server/client_control_handler.go with: handleROCtrl (process control command - READY/EXECUTE/PAUSE/STOP/SIGNAL - update item/story/RO status and publish events), handleROItemCue (process item cue event, log timing info).

5. Create src/internal/server/client_profile6_handler.go with: handleROStorySend (MOS sends story to NCS - store the story body), handleROReqStoryAction (MOS requests story modification from NCS - forward via event bus to NCS clients).

6. For Profile 7 (MOS-initiated modifications): The roElementAction message is already handled from FEAT-003. Profile 7 means the MOS server can also SEND roElementAction messages to NCS clients. Add methods to TCPServer/service that allow the MOS to initiate: SendROElementAction(ctx, clientID, action), SendROStorySend(ctx, clientID, storySend). These use client.Write() to push messages to connected NCS clients.
7. Add service methods: ProcessROCtrl (update status based on command, publish ControlEvent), ProcessROItemCue (log and forward), SendStoryToNCS, InitiateROModification.
8. Add event types: ItemControlled, ItemCued, StoryReceived, ROModificationInitiated in events/bus.go.
9. Update handleMessage type switch for roCtrl, roItemCue, roStorySend, roReqStoryAction.

10. Create src/internal/xml/parser_test.go with unit tests that verify parsing of at least one representative message from each profile (0-7): keepAlive, mosObj, roCreate, mosObjCreate, roElementAction (INSERT), roCtrl, roStorySend, roElementAction (DELETE as Profile 7 example). Each test creates XML bytes, feeds them to the parser, and asserts the correct struct type and field values.
acceptance_criteria: go build -o openmos compiles without errors
go test ./internal/xml/ passes with all parser tests green
Parser recognizes roCtrl, roItemCue, roStorySend, roReqStoryAction
Profile 7 MOS-initiated message sending is available via service/server methods
All 8 profiles (0-7) have their messages defined, parsed, and handled
findings: Addressed 5 review issues: (1) ProcessROCtrl returns error on missing item instead of silent success, (2) Item duration propagated via strconv.Atoi in all element_action INSERT/REPLACE paths, (3) Object ID uses crypto/rand via utils.GenerateID, (4) DeleteStories/DeleteItems use batch DeleteMultiple methods, (5) Parser self-closing tag detection fixed to only match root element. Note: str_replace tool had caching issues - used Python file I/O for reliable edits.
